title: Incoming active slices in symmetric operadic families
statement:
Use symmetric operadic families, active simplices and their inert projections from [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], join slices of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], active concatenation from [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation], and categorical equivalences of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Let $M^\otimes\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^n$ be a small symmetric operadic family, $n\geq1$. Write $M_0^\otimes$ for its fiber at $0$. Let $\sigma:\Delta^r\to M^\otimes$ be an active simplex all of whose vertices have strictly positive $\Delta^n$-coordinate. Put $X=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}M^\otimes_{/\sigma}$, and let $X_{\mathrm{act}}\subseteq X$ be the full subcategory of cones all of whose cross edges are active. The inclusion $X_{\mathrm{act}}\hookrightarrow X$ admits a left adjoint, given by the inert-active factorization of the incoming arrows. Write $J_b=M_0^\otimes\times_{M^\otimes}(M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}})_{/b}$ for an incoming active slice.
For any object $b$ of positive coordinate over $\langle s\rangle$, and chosen inert projections $b\to b_j$, inert-active factorization gives an equivalence
$$J_b\simeq\prod_{j=1}^s J_{b_j}.$$
Under this equivalence the source tuple and the canonical cone to $b$ identify coherently with the concatenation of the source tuples and canonical cones to $b_j$. These identifications persist after applying any inert-preserving family map to a symmetric infinity-operad, including all cocone composition homotopies. For $s=0$ the product is terminal and its tuple is empty.

proof.text:
Put $B=\Delta^n\times N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. The join-slice projection is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; its pullback to the quasicategory $M_0^\otimes$ is again a right fibration directly from the horn-lifting definition in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Hence $X$ is a quasicategory. Restriction to the first vertex of $\sigma$ fixes the entire source simplex and is a trivial Kan fibration by [lem-coef-initial-poset-slice-restriction], applied to the least vertex of $[r]$, first in $M^\otimes$ and then in $M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$. In the second application use its full coordinate-zero subcategory $(M_0^\otimes)_{\mathrm{act}}$. The source coordinate-zero subcategories are full because the parameter simplex has only identity endomorphisms. Also a transformation between active cones has active source edge: its composite with an active edge is active, forcing the source map to send no non-basepoint input to the basepoint. Thus the second slice is exactly $X_{\mathrm{act}}$. The asserted lifting for all monomorphisms gives contractible spaces of compatible first-vertex extensions, including prescribed source triangles and their higher simplices. Mapping spaces may therefore be computed from incoming-arrow triangles by [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space]. Let $C$ have source $x$ over $\langle k\rangle$, and let $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle l\rangle$ underlie its arrow to $\sigma(0)$. Set $D=\{u\ne *:\alpha(u)\ne *\}$. Factor $\alpha$ through the inert projection $\langle k\rangle\to D_+$ followed by the active restriction $D_+\to\langle l\rangle$, where $D_+=D\amalg\{*\}$. This is an explicit factorization of finite pointed maps, not an application of an operad theorem to the total family. By [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], the inert projection has a $\pi$-cocartesian lift $i:x\to x_D$ inside $M_0^\otimes$. Its universal property from [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] factors the first incoming arrow through $x_D$ over the specified factored base arrow. Extend this active incoming arrow over $\sigma$ and the unit triangle by the first-vertex lifting just cited. Its cross edges are active: they compose the active map $D_+\to\langle l\rangle$ with the active base maps of $\sigma$. Write $L(C)$ for this cone, with unit source edge $i$.

For an active cone $A$ with source $y$, a transformation $C\to A$ has a source map $g:x\to y$ whose pointed map $\beta$ satisfies $\alpha_A\beta=\alpha$. Since $\alpha_A$ is active, $\beta$ sends exactly the complement of $D$ to the basepoint, so it factors uniquely through $D_+$. The cocartesian mapping-space square for $i$ identifies the space of such $g$, with its cone homotopy, with the space of maps $x_D\to y$ and the factored cone homotopy. This is an equivalence of full mapping spaces, natural in $A$, not merely a bijection of arrows: take the homotopy fibers specifying the incoming-arrow triangles in [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space] and then the contractible first-vertex extension spaces. It gives $\operatorname{Map}_X(C,A)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{X_{\mathrm{act}}}(L(C),A)$. The dual representability criterion [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-adjoint-criterion] assembles these representing objects into the asserted coherent left adjoint.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications expanded by the second reader.

proof.text:
Construct the output comparison explicitly. Each $J_b$ is the pullback of the right slice of $M^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ to its full coordinate-zero subcategory $(M_0^\otimes)_{\mathrm{act}}$, so its right-fibration base for the mapping-space calculation is this active subcategory. For an active arrow $a:x\to b$ with pointed map $\alpha:\langle k\rangle\to\langle s\rangle$, put $D_j=\alpha^{-1}(j)$ for $1\leq j\leq s$. Activity says that the $D_j$ partition all non-basepoint inputs, including empty blocks. Lift $\langle k\rangle\to(D_j)_+$ inertly at $x$ in $M_0^\otimes$, obtaining $p_j:x\to x_j$. The composite $x\to b\to b_j$ factors through $p_j$, by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], to an active $a_j:x_j\to b_j$. For a triangle $a' h=a$ in $J_b$, its pointed source map $h$ is active and sends $D_j$ into $D'_j$, since $\alpha' h=\alpha$. The composite $p'_j h$ therefore factors through $p_j$ to $h_j:x_j\to x'_j$ with its triangle $a'_j h_j=a_j$. The same cocartesian universal property applies to the mapping spaces of triangles, hence includes their paths and higher simplices. The slice formulas of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] and [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space] identify precisely these coherent triangles and their mapping spaces. Thus this construction gives the comparison $P:J_b\to\prod_jJ_{b_j}$.

For its inverse, start with active $a_j:x_j\to b_j$. Form $x=\bigoplus_jx_j$ in the single operad $M_0^\otimes$, using [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. Its inert projections $p_j$ onto the subtuples exist by [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family]. Define the pointed map $\alpha$ on the concatenated inputs by sending the entire $j$th block to $j$. The relative Segal homotopy-pullback square of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], restricted to the base edge $(0\to t,\alpha)$ for the coordinate $t$ of $b$, identifies arrows $x\to b$ over this edge with the product of arrows $x\to b_j$ over its output composites. Take the components $a_jp_j$. This constructs $a:x\to b$, with a contractible space of choices of the arrow together with these specified component identifications. For source transformations use $\bigoplus_jh_j$, formed in $M_0^\otimes$ by the same concatenation lemma; the component triangles specify the triangle $a'(\bigoplus_jh_j)=a$ under the Segal equivalence. Applying the mapping-space equivalence with its path coordinates gives the transformations and their higher compatibilities, not only their component equations. These natural constructions give $Q:\prod_jJ_{b_j}\to J_b$. No concatenation of cross-parameter arrows in the total family is assumed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications expanded by the second reader.

proof.text: Check the two composites, including the source and cone comparisons. For a tuple $(a_j)$, the blocks of the active pointed map used to define $Q$ are its original input blocks. The projections of $\bigoplus_jx_j$ onto these blocks recover $x_j$ and $a_j$ by the inert cocartesian universal property in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. This gives $PQ\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Conversely, the blocks $\alpha^{-1}(j)$ of an active $a:x\to b$ exhaust its inputs. The fiber Segal axiom for the operad $M_0^\otimes$, as stated in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], reconstructs $x$ from those colors; the symmetric concatenation of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] gives the equivalence $\bigoplus_jx_j\simeq x$, allowing the permutation which puts the blocks consecutively. Under this equivalence, $a$ and the arrow constructed by $Q$ have the same output components $a_jp_j$. The relative Segal equivalence of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] identifies the arrows together with their component homotopies. Naturality of these mapping-space comparisons gives $QP\simeq\mathrm{id}$. The cone mapping formula in [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], applied to the opposite quasicategory so that its left cones are the cocones used here, retains the specified composition paths, so these natural equivalences identify the whole canonical cone, as well as its source diagram. Their components are equivalences by the pointwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The quasi-inverse characterization in [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] now gives the categorical equivalence asserted in the statement.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications expanded by the second reader.

proof.text: Let $F:M^\otimes\to E^\otimes$ be an inert-preserving family map. It preserves all base pointed maps, hence the blocks $D_j$ and activity; by the family-map definition [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] it sends each $p_j$ and each $b\to b_j$ to an inert edge. Consequently the image of the triangle defining $a_j$ is the factorization triangle for $F(a)$ through $F(p_j)$. Its identification with any chosen factorization in $E^\otimes$ is the contractible comparison specified by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. The restriction $F|_{M_0^\otimes}$ is a map of symmetric infinity-operads, so [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation] identifies $F(\bigoplus_jx_j)$ with $\bigoplus_jF(x_j)$ and preserves the symmetry, associativity and unit coherences used in step 3. Each output component of the image cone is $F(a_j)F(p_j)$, with its actual image composition homotopy. The output mapping-space Segal axiom in $E^\otimes$, stated in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], then identifies this image cone with the assembled output cones. Naturality in the ambient quasicategory of the join-cone comparison [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus], applied to opposite quasicategories as in step 3, ensures that these are identifications of diagrams and coherent cones in every simplicial degree. This proves the claimed compatibility after applying $F$; it does not assert that the induced functor from $J_b$ to the active slice in $E^\otimes$ is itself an equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (1), printed pp.336-337; relative factorization, block decomposition, and coherent cone identifications expanded by the second reader.

proof.text: For $s=0$, an active pointed map $\langle k\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$ exists exactly when $k=0$. Thus every object of $J_b$ has the empty source tuple. The zero fiber of $M_0^\otimes$ is a terminal quasicategory up to equivalence by the fiber Segal axiom of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], and it is nonempty. The relative Segal square of [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] at $b$ has a point in both product positions, so its left vertical map is an equivalence. In particular, for each empty-tuple source $x$ its homotopy fiber at the unique base map $(0,\langle0\rangle)\to(t,\langle0\rangle)$ is contractible; hence such incoming arrows exist. For any two such arrows, the space of source maps is contractible and the space of compatible triangles is contractible by [lem-cbc-right-fibration-morphism-space]. Therefore $J_b$ is equivalent to the point, as required for the empty product. The canonical cone still has its apex and the arrow from the empty source tuple; it is not an empty diagram. Its source tuple is the unit of [lem-coef-active-operad-cocartesian-concatenation]. For $s=1$ the only block is the whole input tuple, so $P$ and $Q$ are the identity up to their specified unit coherences. A nullary arrow into a color has an empty block and is retained in step 2, since no block was required nonempty. The proof of step 1 also permits $D=\varnothing$, repeated positive coordinates of $\sigma$, and $r=0$.
